title: Playwriting Group
description: All playwrights welcome! Whether playwriting is new to you or you're already an accomplished playwright, come join this on-going bi-weekly writers' group. We'll spend our time focusing on our writing, but with that magical element of doing so within the presence of others. Come discover the amazing experience of writing within the context of a group. Bring your computer, notebook, iPad, or whatever you like to use for writing. We share resources, discuss our goals and challenges, even provide feedback, but the primary focus of the group is to work on your own play! We'll do a check-in/discussion at the beginning of the meeting, then write in silence, and check-out at the end of our session. Michael Cleveland
venue_name: The Center For The Art - Marissa Funk Theater
description: Weds., September 23, 2026, Doors: 6pm | Show: 7pm, Tickets: Reserved Seating | Genre: Americana, Bluegrass, Roots, Michael Cleveland, widely regarded as the defining bluegrass fiddler of his generation, began performing professionally after high school with Dale Ann Bradley and Rhonda Vincent before forming his own band, Flamekeeper, in 2006—now a seven-time recipient of the IBMA’s Instrumental Group of the Year award. In 2026, he is featured in the Country Music Hall of Fame’s American Currents: State of the Music exhibit, recognizing his ongoing impact on the genre. A twelve-time IBMA Fiddle Player of the Year and 2018 National Fiddlers Hall of Fame inductee, Cleveland has toured and recorded with legendary artists including Béla Fleck, Tommy Emmanuel, Billy Strings, and Vince Gill., He is a four-time GRAMMY® nominee, including a nomination this year for Best Bluegrass Album with Jason Carter for their collaboration Carter & Cleveland, which also won IBMA’s Album of the Year and Song of the Year (“Outrun the Rain”) at this year’s awards. Cleveland previously won a GRAMMY® for Best Bluegrass Album in 2019 for Tall Fiddler, the same year his inspiring journey was chronicled in the documentary Flamekeeper: The Michael Cleveland Story. A recipient of the NEA National Heritage Fellowship, he continues to expand his artistic reach—his masterful fiddle playing can even be heard in the newest season of King of the Hill.

Harlan County, U.S.A.
venue_name: The Onyx Downtown at the Nevada Theatre
description: 9/27 - Presented in a new restoration to mark the film’s 50th anniversary, Barbara Kopple’s Academy Award–winning HARLAN COUNTY USA unflinchingly documents a coal miners’ strike in a small Kentucky town. With unprecedented access, Kopple and her crew captured the miners’ sometimes violent struggles with strikebreakers, local police, and company thugs. With a haunting soundtrack—featuring legendary country and bluegrass artists Hazel Dickens, Merle Travis, David Morris, Sarah Ogan Gunning, and Florence Reece—the film is a heartbreaking record of the thirteen-month struggle between a community fighting to survive and a corporation dedicated to the bottom line.

title: Bill Frisell & Harmony Five
description: Presented by The Center for the Arts , Sun. September 27, 2026, Doors: 6pm | Show: 7pm, Tickets: Reserved Seating | Genre: Americana, Folk, Jazz, One of America's most celebrated guitarists and composers, Bill Frisell brings his newly assembled "Harmony Five" ensemble to the Center for the Arts in a concert celebrating his 75th birthday. Frisell's new album In My Dreams (Blue Note Records, 2026) captures the spirit of this rare gathering - a reunion of his closest long-time collaborators, including cellist Hank Roberts, with whom he shares nearly 50 years of musical history., Rounding out the ensemble are vocalist and multi-instrumentalist Petra Haden (daughter of jazz legend Charlie Haden), guitarist/bassist Luke Bergman, and drummer Timothy Angulo - together bringing a remarkable depth of jazz, Americana, and adventurous improvisation to the stage., "A family gathering. A reunion. That's what it feels like getting together with my closest friends. There's still much unfinished business. We're just getting started." - Bill Frisell

title: Annual Autumn Shindig Fundraiser
description: For the last 17 years or so, the Autumn Shindig on the San Juan Ridge has been a reliable harbinger of fall. An annual event to benefit the North Columbia Schoolhouse Cultural Center, this fun and family-friendly festival features live music, local crafts, games for kids and adults alike, and various contests., The festival is a daytime affair beginning at 11:30 am and going until dusk. Admission for the festival is free. Attendees purchase rustic wooden tokens to spend on the food and game booths. Local craftspeople and farmers will also have booths with goods on sale., Gourmet harvest stew, garden salad and fresh bread will be available thanks to local farms, as well as other generous business donations. There will be comfort food and drinks, and organic cotton candy at The “Sugar Shack” which will host the Great Shindig Bake-off with prizes as well as serving Organic cotton Candy and other sweets in all shapes and sizes. 3 Forks Brewery will have local brew on tap., The variety of local live music throughout the day include Oliah Fall, The Heifer Belles, Awkward Pocket, & Delphine & The Moss Collective & more TBA…. The musicians all generously sponsor the event by playing pro bono., Enter the Sack Race just by showing up by 12:30. Grow out your hair and win a prize for the Best Beard, or burn your mouth in the Hot Pepper Eating Contest!, Longtime supporters Mother Truckers & Natural Selection along with Three Forks Bakery & Brewery are sponsoring the Shindig. Many other local businesses provide additional sponsorship to keep this treasure of the San Juan Ridge vibrant and healthy.,

title: Marty Stuart and his Fabulous Superlatives
venue_name: The Center For The Arts - Marissa Funk Theater
description: He's been playing country music for fifty years. Then he went to Capitol Records in Hollywood, picked up Clarence White's Telecaster, and made twenty instrumentals. No vocals. No precedent. Just Marty Stuart and The Fabulous Superlatives doing something they had never done before., Doors at 6:00 PM, showtime at 7:00 PM., The new album, Space Junk, was recorded at the legendary Capitol Recording Studios — the same room where The Beach Boys, Ray Charles, and Buck Owens made their records. The cover art is a painting by Herb Alpert, who personally consented to its use. Stuart played Clarence White's actual Fender Telecaster on the track "California Part 1 (Bobbie Gentry Please Call Home).", This is not a nostalgia show. This is a five-time GRAMMY winner and Country Music Hall of Famer in the middle of something genuinely new. In a 500-seat room.

description: Paula Cole returns to the stage with THIS FIRE: 30—a special anniversary tour celebrating three decades of This Fire. A Grammy-winning singer-songwriter known for her fearless writing and genre-blending sound, Cole broke boundaries with songs that were both deeply personal and universally resonant. On THIS FIRE: 30, Paula will perform This Fire in its entirety—revisiting the era-defining music that sparked a generation and bringing new life, nuance, and power to the songs fans have carried with them for decades. Expect an intimate, emotionally charged performance that honors the original spirit of the album while showcasing the artistry and perspective she’s continued to evolve.

title: SPACETIME: The Universe Story and Our Place In It at The Center for the Arts
description: SPACETIME is a captivating live performance that brings the wonders of the universe to life through storytelling, music, science, and breathtaking imagery. Join acclaimed storyteller David González, astrophysicist Dr. Luke Keller, and guitarist-composer Álvaro Domene on an unforgettable journey from the birth of the cosmos to our shared human story. Blending discovery, imagination, and awe, SPACETIME invites audiences of all ages to look up, wonder, and reconnect with the extraordinary universe we call home., Perfect for curious minds, science enthusiasts, art lovers, and anyone who has ever gazed at the stars and asked, “How did we get here?”

title: Those Darn Accordions At The Nevada Theatre
description: Those Darn Accordions bring their high-energy accordion-fueled rock & roll to the historic Nevada Theatre October 9, NEVADA CITY, CA — Think you know what an accordion sounds like? Think again., San Francisco’s legendary accordion-rockers Those Darn Accordions are ready to rock Nevada City when they take the stage at the historic Nevada Theatre on Friday, October 9., Fronted by singer, songwriter and accordionist Paul Rogers, Those Darn Accordions have spent decades proving that the accordion can be much more than a polka instrument. With four accordion players up front, backed by bass and drums, the band delivers a wild mix of rock, funk, ska, country, polka and straight-ahead good-time music—with plenty of humor and showmanship thrown in., The result is a live show unlike anything else on the musical landscape: six musicians creating a surprisingly big, driving sound while four accordions trade riffs, melodies and musical punches across the front of the stage., Those Darn Accordions aren't newcomers to the national stage. The band has appeared on The American Music Awards with Drew Carey, Good Morning America, MTV Rock N' Jock, Donny & Marie, Penn & Teller's Sin City Spectacular and other television programs. Their music and antics have also been featured in Time, People and Entertainment Weekly., But at the heart of Those Darn Accordions is a simple idea: accordions are cool—and they can rock., “People have a certain idea of what an accordion band is supposed to sound like,” says Rogers. “Then we hit them with four accordions, bass and drums.”, The band's Nevada City appearance brings its famously energetic live show to one of Northern California's most historic venues. The Nevada Theatre, dating to 1865, provides a fitting setting for a band that has spent years taking something old-fashioned and turning it completely upside down.
